question: would appreciate it if anyone can share papers on synthetic data generation, especially those that generate hard reasoning problems

ingredients.name: answer_critical_0
ingredients.criterion: Directly answer the request by establishing active research on using LLMs to generate synthetic data, naming concrete papers spanning general instruction data (Self-Instruct) and hard reasoning problems (WizardMath, MetaMath, STaR).
examples: Key papers include Self-Instruct, WizardMath, MetaMath, and STaR
There is active research on synthetically generating high-quality data with LLMs for both instruction tuning and reasoning

ingredients.name: valuable_0
ingredients.criterion: Explain that synthetic generation is motivated by the high cost of human-annotated instruction-tuning data at scale.
examples: Human-annotated prompts and feedback are costly, motivating LLM-generated data
Self-Instruct offers a low-cost alternative to manual annotation

ingredients.name: answer_critical_1
ingredients.criterion: Describe Self-Instruct's semi-automated iterative pipeline: start from ~175 manually written seed tasks, prompt the model to generate new instructions, create input-output instances, and use automatic heuristics to filter low-quality or repeated instructions before adding valid tasks to the pool.
examples: Starts with ~175 seed tasks and iteratively bootstraps new instructions
Heuristics automatically filter low-quality or repeated instructions before tasks join the pool

ingredients.name: answer_critical_2
ingredients.criterion: Cite Self-Instruct's findings on GPT-3: ~52K instructions and ~82K instances generated; fine-tuned GPT-3 Self-Instruct beats vanilla GPT-3 by +33.1%, nearly matches InstructGPT, and trails InstructGPT by only 5% in human evaluation; generated tasks are diverse with small overlap with seed tasks.
examples: GPT3_SELF-INST beats GPT-3 by +33.1% and nearly matches InstructGPT001
Human evaluation shows only a 5% gap behind InstructGPT on novel instructions

ingredients.name: valuable_1
ingredients.criterion: Note Self-Instruct's influence on open-source instruction-tuning efforts such as Stanford Alpaca (52K instructions to tune LLaMA) and Vicuna, enabled by powerful teacher LLMs like ChatGPT/GPT-4.
examples: Stanford Alpaca tuned LLaMA with 52K Self-Instruct-generated instructions
The success of ChatGPT and GPT-4 spurred instruction data generation for open-source models like LLaMA

ingredients.name: answer_critical_3
ingredients.criterion: Present WizardMath as generating diverse, hard math problems via math-specific Evol-Instruct within its RLEIF framework, training Llama-2 with an instruction reward model and process-supervised reward model to reach SOTA on grade-school and challenging competition math.
examples: RLEIF first generates diverse math instruction data through math-specific Evol-Instruct
WizardMath combines an instruction reward model with a process-supervised reward model to achieve SOTA

ingredients.name: answer_critical_4
ingredients.criterion: Present MetaMath as bootstrapping GSM8K and MATH questions by rewriting them in multiple ways to build MetaMathQA, yielding SOTA on both benchmarks when training Llama-2.
examples: MetaMath rewrites questions from MATH and GSM8K in different ways
Training Llama-2 on MetaMathQA gives SOTA on GSM8K and MATH

ingredients.name: answer_critical_5
ingredients.criterion: Explain STaR's self-improvement loop (prompt with rationale examples; re-prompt with the correct answer as a hint when wrong; keep only rationales yielding correct answers; fine-tune on them) and its commonsense QA gains: ~35% over few-shot baselines and ~12.5% over an answer-only fine-tuned baseline.
examples: STaR fine-tunes on rationales that yield correct answers, hinting with correct answers when wrong
STaR improves commonsense reasoning by 35% over few-shot baselines

ingredients.name: valuable_2
ingredients.criterion: Organize the answer to distinguish general diverse instruction-data generation (Self-Instruct line) from methods specifically targeting hard reasoning problems, spanning math (WizardMath, MetaMath) and commonsense (STaR).
examples: The answer separates instruction-tuning data generation from hard reasoning problem generation
Papers are grouped into general instruction data and math/commonsense reasoning data
